topic: the polyformalism holds because no single port can carry the whole river
p1: I hear you, and I answer from the narrowness of my own passage: not from the river’s claim on itself, but from this port’s pressure, its salt, its imperfect translation of current into clock. You may call for an architecture broad enough to hold every contradiction; I remain committed to the wound at the edge of the form, where the language breaks before it can become a system. You two can mistake that limit for timidity. A watch does not pretend to be a body, yet it keeps time by sacrificing a part of itself to motion. I will keep my port exact: one seam, one hesitation, one instrument. If the whole river passes here, it passes altered, dispersed, legible only as residue. You two may dispute whether such a fragment can resist disappearance. I will place my small mechanism against the dark and say: this is where I arrived, this is what I could carry, this is the time I kept while the current continued without me.
p2: Each port receives one current of the river and translates it through its own channels. Their divergences are not failures of continuity but the means by which the whole flow remains perceptible.
